draft.title: Vector equation of a line
card: A line in space is set by one point on it and a direction. The vector equation is r = a + tb.
a
the position vector of a known point on the line.
b
a direction vector, which is parallel to the line. Any non-zero multiple of b gives the same direction.
t
a real number that can be positive, negative or zero. Each value of t gives one point on the line.
draft.remember: Start at a, then move any number t of steps along b.

a.q: A line has the equation r = (3i − j + 2k) + t(i + 4j − k). Which point is on the line when t = 2?
a.why: When t = 2, r = (3i − j + 2k) + 2(i + 4j − k) = 5i + 7j + 0k. The point (5, 8, −2) comes from adding 2 to a instead of adding 2b, so it is wrong.
a.clue: Multiply every part of b by 2, then add a.

b.q: Which is a vector equation of the line through A(1, 2, 0) and B(4, 6, 12)?
b.why: The direction is B − A = (3, 4, 12), and A is a point on the line. Using the position vector of B as the direction is tempting, but that vector is not parallel to the line, since the line does not pass through the origin.
b.clue: Find the direction by subtracting one point from the other.

problems.detail: Why (a) says (5, 8, −2) comes from adding 2 to a instead of adding 2b. Adding 2 to each part of a gives (5, 1, 4), not (5, 8, −2). The explanation of this distractor is wrong and would confuse a student checking their error.

check.summary: Both questions have exactly one correct answer: (5, 7, 0) and r = (i + 2j) + t(3i + 4j + 12k). Why (a) wrongly says the distractor (5, 8, −2) comes from adding 2 to a, which actually gives (5, 1, 4).

proposal.title: Vector equation of a line
card: A line in space is set by one point on it and a direction. The vector equation is r = a + tb.
a
the position vector of a known point on the line.
b
a direction vector, parallel to the line. For points A and B on the line, b = B − A works. Any non-zero multiple of b gives the same direction.
t
a real number that can be positive, negative or zero. Each value of t gives one point on the line.
proposal.remember: Start at a, then move any number t of steps along b.

a.q: A line has the equation r = (3i − j + 2k) + t(i + 4j − k). Which point is on the line when t = 2?
a.why: When t = 2, r = (3i − j + 2k) + 2(i + 4j − k) = 5i + 7j + 0k, so the point is (5, 7, 0). The point (4, 3, 1) is where t = 1, and (5, 9, 0) comes from reading −j in a as +j.
a.clue: Multiply every part of b by 2, then add a.

b.q: Which is a vector equation of the line through A(1, 2, 0) and B(4, 6, 12)?
b.why: The direction is B − A = (3, 4, 12), and A is a point on the line. Using the position vector of B as the direction is tempting, but (4, 6, 12) is not a multiple of (3, 4, 12), so it is not parallel to the line.
b.clue: Find the direction by subtracting one point from the other.
